title: COMPLETE-from-a-dep does NOT release that dep's pending DIRTY contribution (wedges a multi-dep node): a dep that emits DIRTY then COMPLETE WITHOUT an intervening DATA/RESOLVED leaves _depDirty[idx]=true and _pending>0 — the INVALIDATE arm clears this (EC3) but the COMPLETE/ERROR arms do not. A multi-dep node (e.g. deps [D,E], D dirties then completes, E live) then has _pending stuck >0 → _maybeRun/_tryRun is gated forever → the node never recomputes or settles. NOT hit by the normal inner lifecycle (sources emit DATA-then-COMPLETE, or bare COMPLETE with no prior DIRTY), so the *Map first cut is unaffected.

title: graphrefly-rs DeferredCtx holds a STRONG Core (Rc<RefCell<NodeInner>>): an async fn that stashes ctx.defer() and never emits (abandoned/cancelled work, a never-resolving backend) pins the node's NodeInner — and thus its fn slot (blocking the B32 unregister), its captured upstream Cores, and its dep_unsubs subscriptions — alive until the DeferredCtx drops. In correct usage the DeferredCtx drops when the async work completes/aborts (no leak), and the strong hold MATCHES TS's GC-reachability (the async callback closure keeps the TS node alive until it resolves). But it makes the dispatcher invoke's stale-handle no-op comment unreachable for this path (a strong Core can't have dropped+recycled), and a switchMap-style cancel that drops the DeferredCtx late over-retains until then
trigger: the real async-pool runner lands (B1) — decide strong-vs-Weak hold for DeferredCtx. Weak<RefCell<NodeInner>> (upgrade at emit, drop silently if gone — matching the dep-sink discipline) makes Drop/B32 reachable + the stale-handle no-op real, but silently drops an async result if the Node handle was dropped first (arguably wrong for an async source you want the result from). Surfaced by the CSP-6 Slice A /qa (2026-05-30, Blind Hunter). Low urgency: no leak in correct usage, no conformance path; revisit with the async runner.

title: PROTOCOL-PULL design question (Fork B blocker, deferred to a NEW /design-review session): should GraphReFly add a protocol-level PULL -- a DEMAND/REQUEST tier (the callbag type-1-up analogue) so a sink can REQUEST data UP the conveyor belt and the source responds with DATA DOWN on demand, creating a DECLARED, inspectable pull-edge? USER'S LOAD-BEARING FRAMING (reframes the naive view): a PROTOCOL pull HONORS the guard -- a declared DEMAND edge appears in describe (D3/L0.7 inspectable topology satisfied); whereas the EXISTING method-pull (node.cache / lineage get()) is the actual BYPASS -- an invisible side-channel read outside the protocol. So 'pull breaks inspectability' is TRUE ONLY for method-pull (.cache); a declared protocol-pull is inspectable. LINEAGE: raw callbag HAS talkback pull (sink sends type-1-up no-payload = 'give me' -> source sends type-1-down = value; same type-1 both directions); callbag-recharge (the foundation GraphReFly is built on) ALREADY dropped it -- REFLOW-SPEC §1.4 up = PAUSE/RESUME/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN (control only), chose METHOD-pull node.get() (cached read, MAY recompute-when-disconnected) over message-pull because of F-SYNC-CORE (message-pull is an async-style request/response round-trip, awkward in a sync wave core; get() is synchronous recursive DAG eval, glitch-free by construction); clean-slate inherited this (.cache = renamed get(), node.ts:200; R-data-not-peek scopes .cache to EXTERNAL consumers, bans in-graph .cache-peek to keep topology inspectable).
resolution: RESOLVED 2026-05-30 by D55: NO new DEMAND tier. Protocol-pull is realized as a SUBSTRATE pull-mode node (NodeOptions.pull:true) reusing RESUME as the demand + the D47 wave-boundary for self-demands. The naive design wedged downstream (a quiet compute node relayed phase-1 DIRTY but withheld the settle) -- the fix is quiet-DIRTY ABSORPTION + no-push-on-subscribe + deferred demand; spike-verified (_probe-pull P0b/P4/P5). pull:true -> R-pull/wave_pull.tla/C-1x via /spec-amend; reactiveList two-port (stream push + snapshot pull) is per-language. DESIGN CHALLENGES dissolved: no DAG pull-coordination (demand targets one cache-warm source), no F-SYNC-CORE round-trip (synchronous cache-warm flush), no constitutional D9 change.
trigger: DONE -- /spec-amend (B) pending to land R-pull. Original trigger (for record): a fresh /decision-guard -> /design-review -> (if approved) /spec-amend to assess 'how much trouble vs how much benefit' of protocol-pull. BLOCKERS to amend: D9 (closed 9-tier set has NO DEMAND/REQUEST tier -- 'adding a tier is a constitutional change') + D8/R-ctx-up (up = control-tier only). DESIGN CHALLENGES to assess: (1) DAG pull-coordination -- a sink D pulling through a diamond (B,C over A): request fan-out, response fan-in, compute-A-once memoization; (2) F-SYNC-CORE reconciliation -- a synchronous request/response round-trip in the sync wave core (the reason the lineage chose method-pull); (3) interaction with two-phase push + ROM/RAM caching + lazy activation (does protocol-pull COMPLEMENT push or REPLACE part of it?); (4) tier/wave semantics (is DEMAND its own tier? how does it coexist with DIRTY/DATA?). BENEFITS to weigh: inspectable on-demand pull (vs the invisible .cache bypass), restored callbag pull/push duality, lazy eval through the protocol, a cleaner reactiveCollection (delta-stream push + snapshot pull ALL through the belt -- no external .cache side-channel). GATES Fork B (CSP-2.8 data-structures emit/delivery shape): whether reactiveCollection's snapshot is delivered via lazy-push items (no protocol change) OR a protocol-pull determines the emit design. Until resolved, Fork B (D55) is NOT locked; CSP-2.8 data-structures is ~90% designed (Fork A=D54 locked, shared scan-accumulator core + mechanical dissolutions set, composition=D56, storage=D57, render mechanical) with ONLY the snapshot-delivery/emit shape pending on this.

title: single-dep transform/take operators read ctx.depRecords[0].latest (last-of-batch), NOT iterate .batch -- so under a COALESCED multi-DATA batch they see only the last value + counters under-count. Affects map/filter/scan/distinctUntilChanged (pre-existing since CSP-2.6) + the CSP-2.7 additions skip/take/takeWhile/first/pairwise; contrast reduce/last/find/elementAt/tap/settle/merge/bufferCount which DO iterate r.batch. Surfaced by the CSP-2.7 /qa (Blind Hunter + Edge Case Hunter). REACHABILITY is narrow: for a SINGLE dep, _depBatch only accumulates >1 value before one fn run via pause-coalescing (R-pause-modes default mode = fire-once-with-latest-on-RESUME, where latest-only is the SPEC'd behavior, NOT a bug) or a first-run-gate-held / diamond-gated window; in the normal one-DATA-per-wave path each DATA drives its own _runWave (node.ts:886 resets _depBatch), so .latest == the only value. So this is an INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY + D49-occurrence-fidelity observation, NOT a confirmed correctness bug (the only reachable multi-batch path is pause-coalescing, which is latest-only by R-pause-modes).
trigger: RESOLVED 2026-06-01 (@graphrefly/ts). Reopen only if a new operator deliberately chooses coalesced-latest semantics over occurrence semantics, or if a pause-coalescing-specific counting policy is introduced.
resolved_by: TS operators.ts batch-first single-dep occurrence handling + regression coverage
resolution: Single-dep transform/take operators now consume depRecords[0].batch occurrences instead of depRecords[0].latest for map/filter/scan/distinctUntilChanged/skip/take/takeWhile/first/pairwise. This aligns operator counting with D49 occurrence semantics, prevents stale re-emits on undirty RESOLVED-only waves (no fresh DATA), and handles in-wave multi-DATA batches deterministically. Regression tests were added in operators.test.ts for in-batch occurrence behavior and RESOLVED no-stale-reemit behavior.

title: RxJS-7 time-operator complete-edge reference (context7-verified /reactivex/rxjs 7.8.2, 2026-05-30) -- pins the per-operator source-COMPLETE behavior so it is settled BEFORE implementation, NOT left to discover. (A) DEFERRED ops (B41), the behavior to MATCH when authored: audit/auditTime -> FLUSH the pending latest value on source COMPLETE (RxJS 6->7 CHANGE: v6 dropped it, v7 emits the last value; the frozen pure-ts audit also flushes -> agree, author with flush-on-complete). bufferTime -> FLUSH the final buffer on COMPLETE (RxJS 7 'final buffered values are always emitted'; matches the LANDED buffer/bufferCount which already flush remainder + COMPLETE). timeout -> NO flush edge (it ERRORs only on an idle gap > ms; a normal source COMPLETE just forwards COMPLETE). (B) LANDED ops -- known RxJS DIVERGENCES (acceptable, recorded): debounce/debounceTime (switchMap+timer) emits its pending trailing value at (last-value-time + ms) when the in-flight timer fires -- RxJS debounceTime instead FLUSHES the pending value IMMEDIATELY at source-COMPLETE time (its _complete calls debouncedNext() before complete()). So if the source completes mid-window, RxJS emits the trailing value at complete-time; this impl emits it ms later (the *Map+timer composition cannot flush early without detecting COMPLETE inside the switchMap inner -- inherent to the declarative composition). throttle/throttleTime is leading-ONLY (matches RxJS default leading:true/trailing:false) but does NOT expose the leading/trailing options RxJS provides (a capability gap, not a divergence).
trigger: B41 time-tail implementation is DONE. Reopen only if a consumer hits a remaining RxJS divergence/capability gap: debounce/debounceTime flushes pending trailing value at timer-fire time rather than immediately on source COMPLETE; throttle/throttleTime exposes only the RxJS default leading:true/trailing:false shape. Per-language (D6/D24), NO /spec-amend.
resolution: Reference behavior was applied to the landed B41 tail: audit/auditTime flush pending latest on source COMPLETE; bufferTime flushes final buffer on COMPLETE; timeout forwards normal source COMPLETE without error. Remaining divergence/capability notes stay trigger-gated in this backlog row.

title: Rust perf track toward the Stage-3 ceiling (DR-7+DR-8): de-erasure (hybrid typed-internal / erased-boundary) THEN arena + index/generational handles -- move the hot path off Rc<RefCell> (refcount + dynamic-borrow tax) onto arena-owned nodes addressed by index handles (the dispatcher slotmap pattern B32, generalized to the node graph). Beats both Rc<RefCell> and a GC; reclaims the CPU edges where Rust structurally beats TS (GC/alloc, cache-bound, integer/bit, cold-start, polymorphic-no-deopt, SIMD, latency). Probes (crates/graphrefly/examples/perf_probe.rs + perf-probes/ts_probe.mjs) are AUTHORED but NOT RUN.
trigger: Runs IN PARALLEL with the ongoing TS implementation (DR-8 scheduling). STEPS: (a) RUN the authored probes for REAL numbers (own-measurement was deferred) + add a Python/GIL + arena-vs-GC + complex-marshal probe; (b) de-erasure per DR-7 (hybrid) keeping the conformance arm C-2..C-15 GREEN (D24 behavior-preserving); (c) arena+index refactor; stop at the ceiling-ratio target (within 1.5-2x of hand-rolled, near-linear core scaling). Per-language (F-PERF/L5-Q1), NO spec-amend.
note: 2026-06-01 baseline probes rerun on same host (10 cores visible). Rust DR-7 perf_probe (dev): Probe A typed 158.0 ms vs erased 1430.6 ms over 16,000,000 value ops => erasure tax 9.05x (+805%). Probe B ceiling (N=40,W=10,000,000): 1-thread 6658.3 ms, 10-thread 1289.2 ms => 5.16x speedup (52% efficiency), single-thread constant-factor 16.646 ns/iter. TS probe (node v26.0.0, same N/W): 1-thread 2852.7 ms, 10-worker 834.9 ms => 3.42x speedup (34% efficiency), single-thread constant-factor 7.132 ns/iter. Interpretation: Rust parallel scaling headroom looks better, but current erased-path single-thread constant factor is slower than TS in this synthetic loop; this keeps B45/B49 priority on de-erasure + arena bookkeeping before claiming runtime wins.

title: R-pull DEMAND-TRIGGER surface + routing (the per-language trigger of a pull demand, NOT the delivery). User (CSP-2.8 /dev-dispatch+/qa 2026-05-30) prefers NOT a new ctx.demandNext API but a CONE-PROPAGATING ctx.up([[RESUME, lock_id]]): the RESUME travels UP the declared dep-cone like DIRTY does and STOPS at the node holding that lock (the pull:true node / source), which fires DATA down -- so the demand follows DECLARED edges (inspectable). The landed TS impl instead uses DIRECT-TARGET: ctx.demandNext(dep) (a new ctx affordance) / node.up([[RESUME, node.demandLock]]) calls _up on the pull node itself; _up handles PAUSE/RESUME LOCALLY and does NOT propagate them up the cone (only DIRTY/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN propagate). Folds in 3 QA findings the routing model resolves: (F3) demandNext does not verify dep is a DECLARED dep -- a non-pull dep is a silent no-op (no typo signal) and a non-dep pull node can be demanded, creating an undeclared (uninspectable) demand edge -- contradicts the user's own declared-edge-not-.cache-bypass principle; (F4/F5) a demand coinciding with an EXTERNAL pause lock is LOST -- the per-node demand lock shares the single _pauseLockset with ordinary PAUSE locks, so a RESUME(demandLock) with another lock still held early-returns without servicing and drops the lock (pull x pausable not truly orthogonal -- entangled through one Set); (B1/F6) an owed demand (pin 5, demand-while-_pending>0) is STRANDED/misfired when the in-flight dep settles via INVALIDATE or COMPLETE/ERROR -- those receive-arms drain _pending without calling _fireOwedDemandIfReady (only the DATA/RESOLVED arms do). The DELIVERY behavior (quiet-absorb-DIRTY / no-push-on-subscribe / fire-once-DIRTY-before-DATA / re-quiet / true=latest, resumeAll=backlog) is UNAFFECTED and stays conformant -- R-pull ACTIVE + C-16 ts:pass + wave_pull.tla stand; only C-16's (defer)/(immediate) facets and the trigger surface would change.
trigger: A /design-review to LOCK the demand-trigger routing model (cone-propagate-RESUME vs direct-target), reconciling: (1) per-node-lock precision (D55 (d)) -- cone-propagation still needs the lock id, so the consumer needs the pull node's demandLock either way; (2) the SELF-demand D37 deferral (R-pull / R-rewire-deferred) -- ctx.up is IMMEDIATE, so a self-read demand via it re-enters (D37); a deferred path is still required regardless of name; (3) whether _up should propagate RESUME up the cone (stop-at-holder) -- this CHANGES control-message routing in _up (today PAUSE/RESUME are node-local; DIRTY/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN propagate) and interacts with how PAUSE targets a node, so it is a WAVE-PROTOCOL behavior change -> /spec-amend (clarify R-ctx-up routing + possibly R-pause-lockset PAUSE/RESUME targeting; R-pull's routing semantic (d)); (4) make the demand a DECLARED, inspectable edge (resolve F3) and decide demandNext-on-non-pull = throw vs no-op; (5) separate the demand lock from _pauseLockset (or route owed-demand through it) to make pull x pausable orthogonal (resolve F4/F5) and wire _fireOwedDemandIfReady into the INVALIDATE/terminal settle paths (resolve B1/F6). Then re-implement the trigger surface + add C-16 routing/cross-axis facets (demand-up-the-cone, demand x external-PAUSE, demand x INVALIDATE/terminal) and model in wave_pull.tla if routing becomes spec.
resolution: RESOLVED by D59 (RESUME-routed pull: pullId + R-up-routing release-if-held-else-forward-up + ctx.upNext deferred self-demand, drop ctx.demandNext) + the TS impl 2026-05-31. F3 (declared-edge) -> demand routes the DECLARED cone (inspectable); F4/F5 (demand x external PAUSE) + B1/F6 (owed-demand on INVALIDATE/terminal) -> unified _demandOwed serviced across all settle/resume paths (_onDemand/_canFireDemand/_deliverPullDemand + _fireOwedDemandIfReady in DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/terminal arms + _pauseRelease). C-16 ts:pass (routing facets) + wave_pull_routing.tla TLC-green (RoutedResumeReachesHolder + DisambiguatesSiblings, both mutation-verified). rust=CSP-6 / py=CSP-7.

title: R-up-routing: a BROADCAST routed RESUME (no towardDep) over a DIAMOND (the pullId-holder reachable from one demander via 2+ declared paths) invokes the holder's _onDemand ONCE PER PATH. Harmless TODAY -- the 1st delivers, the 2nd is SILENT (true mode: _pausedDepWaveOccurred cleared by the 1st; resumeAll: buffer already drained), so net delivery is 1 (1:1 preserved by COALESCING, not by routing). wave_pull_routing.tla models a strict TREE (G->{F,H}, distinct holders), so the impl diverges from the model in a diamond-to-single-holder topology. _forwardUp (node.ts) broadcasts to all deps with NO visited-set; adding one would also change the PRE-EXISTING DIRTY/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN up-broadcast (idempotent today) -> out of scope for the D59 QA. Surfaced by the D59 /qa (3 reviewers).
trigger: Before a MULTI-PATH pull consumer ships (a pullId-holder reachable from one demander via 2+ declared paths). The reactiveList Fork-B snapshot is single-holder/tree, so NOT hit today. Then: add a per-routed-wave visited / already-demanded guard (or make _onDemand idempotent within one routed RESUME), + a diamond facet to C-16 + a diamond topology in wave_pull_routing.tla asserting fire-once.

title: RESOLVED 2026-05-31: D61 pull snapshot-prep TTL prune delta edge fixed in @graphrefly/ts by splitting reactiveMap into internal mutationDelta + internal pull snapshotPrep + public delta/snapshot declared deps.
trigger: RESOLVED. Reopen only if a later collection core unification removes the snapshotPrep split or if another structure needs snapshot-prep side-effect deltas.
resolution: snapshotPrep(pullId) depends on internal mutationDelta, prunes expired entries and emits an internal {snapshot, expired[]} payload on demand. Public snapshot depends on snapshotPrep and forwards snapshot. Public delta depends on [mutationDelta, snapshotPrep] and forwards normal mutation changes plus snapshotPrep expired deletes. Backend remains the single materialized state; no snapshot fn drives its own dep, so D37 reentrancy is avoided; D61 snapshot-prep expired deletes enter the public delta stream.

title: Rust-first centralized wave bookkeeping / thin Node view probe (may land pre-1.0 per D71 if clean): investigate moving per-node depRecords, pending counts, dirty/terminal dep-slot state, output-slot/wave scratch, internal sinks, and rewire queues into a GraphCore/PropagationEngine arena with CSR adjacency + sparse frontier indexes. User insight 2026-06-01: bookkeeping is the main opportunity; sparse frontier propagation is a useful side-effect, not the primary goal. Preserve graph-first GraphSpec/describe and public API; users should observe only performance, memory, and profiling improvements, not a different programming model. Node becomes a handle/view over graphCore+nodeId with public cache/status/up/down/subscribe affordances; ctx.depRecords remains a logical contract, likely implemented as a lazy view over arrays, and record object identity should not be promised. Optional sidecars stay allocation-on-use: ctx.state, pause buffers/locks, replay buffers, cleanup hooks, external subscribers. Must preserve observable protocol: DIRTY-before-DATA, diamond exactly-once, INVALIDATE dedupe, push-on-subscribe, PAUSE/RESUME, terminal propagation, rewire dep-slot semantics. Avoid double-write designs: either keep current per-node state, or centralize it; do not add frontier indexes while retaining full Node bookkeeping as a second source of truth.
trigger: D71 authorizes Rust as the pre-1.0 proving ground: start with probes that compare current Rust Node/Core objects vs GraphCore arena/CSR/typed-array or slot-array state for DIRTY/INVALIDATE frontier traversal, diamond pending resolution, rewire churn, subscriber fanout, cache locality, and retained heap. If probe data shows clear performance/memory/profile wins without conformance-observable drift, Rust may land B49 before 1.0. TS continues D40/D41 intent migration; D32 remains locked, so other language packages do not become Rust substrate bindings without a separate future decision. No spec-amend if behavior is preserved; if ctx.depRecords identity/timing, wave ordering, describe/GraphSpec observability, or any protocol behavior changes, route through design/spec first.
note: 2026-06-01 Rust D71 first mainline B49 slice landed and passed QA in @graphrefly/rust: Core is now a graph-local arena slot handle (GraphCore + NodeId + external checked refcount) instead of Rc<RefCell<NodeInner>>. Full cargo fmt --all --check is blocked only by pre-existing formatting in crates/graphrefly/examples/perf_probe.rs. Next slices: centralize dep-slot arrays/frontier bookkeeping instead of keeping NodeInner as the slot payload; then measure B49/B45 cache locality, dirty/invalidate traversal, diamond pending, rewire churn, subscriber fanout, and retained heap. title: RESOLVED Rust ready-run frontier A/B: do not land a sparse frontier index that queues ready-to-run nodes while keeping the existing per-message subscriber cascade as the source of truth.
trigger: RESOLVED 2026-06-02. Reopen only if a future B49 slice moves dirty/invalidate traversal into a true centralized adjacency/frontier structure instead of wrapping ready-run execution with an extra queue.
resolution: Implemented a behavior-preserving GraphCore ready_frontier prototype with weak Core tokens and dense queued bits, then rejected it by same-host release perf. It passed 32 unit + 22 conformance after preserving immediate D49 occurrence timing and D37 feedback-cycle detection, but b49_probe showed no clear win: fanout and diamond hot paths regressed while invalidate-only improved only modestly/noisily. The patch was reverted. Final release baseline after revert/package rename: queue Vec/remove(0)=59.935 ms vs VecDeque=0.421 ms; fanout 512x2000=320.725 ms; invalidate-only estimate=33.213 ms; diamond 128x2000=127.138 ms; sparse frontier proxy=0.421 ms; retained heap=5.707 ms/round; rewire churn=17.374 ms. Conclusion: sparse/frontier remains worth pursuing only as a real dirty/INVALIDATE adjacency/workset centralization, not as a ready-run queue layered over existing bookkeeping.

title: RESOLVED Rust INVALIDATE-only centralized adjacency A/B: do not land a partial B-path that adds GraphCore out_edges while retaining internal subscriber closures for the other tiers.
trigger: RESOLVED 2026-06-02. Reopen only as a post-1.0 C-path/full PropagationEngine design, or as a no-double-bookkeeping internal-edge rewrite that removes closure subscribers entirely without changing conformance behavior.
resolution: Per user direction, attempted B = internal GraphCore adjacency for INVALIDATE while leaving DATA/DIRTY/RESOLVED on existing internal subscriber closures. First implementation passed 32 unit + 22 conformance but regressed release b49_probe: invalidate-only ~40.609 ms vs same-window baseline ~31.316 ms, retained-heap proxy ~9.619 ms/round vs ~6.062 ms. Optimized obvious implementation tax (O(1) swap-remove internal-edge deletion and no external-observer fast path) and still failed same-window A/B: patch run invalidate-only ~34.004 ms, rewire ~18.124 ms; baseline run invalidate-only ~30.448 ms, rewire ~16.366 ms. The code patch was reverted. Conclusion: partial B is a double-bookkeeping design and does not satisfy F-PERF. C remains post-1.0: a full centralized PropagationEngine/settle frontier may be reconsidered only with no duplicated internal subscriber path and with conformance-preserving DATA occurrence, diamond, reentrancy, rewire, pause, and terminal semantics.

title: RESOLVED Rust C-propagation replacement probe: do not land a first-cut GraphCore internal adjacency transport that replaces subscriber closures but still delivers per-message with weak-edge sorting/token checks.
trigger: RESOLVED 2026-06-02. Reopen only as a substantially different post-1.0 PropagationEngine design that centralizes scheduling/frontier settlement rather than merely translating the existing per-message cascade into GraphCore out_edges.
resolution: Implemented an experimental C replacement on branch codex/c-propagation-probe: GraphCore owned internal out_edges with weak dst handles and dep-index tokens, internal node-to-node delivery stopped using subscriber closures as the main path, external subscribe()/observe sinks remained closure-based, and fn invocation still went only through dispatcher.invoke. The patch preserved conformance-visible behavior (cargo test -p graphrefly-rs: 32 unit + 22 conformance pass) but failed the same-session release perf gate. Baseline before patch: queue Vec/remove(0)=61.384 ms vs VecDeque=0.426 ms; fanout 512x2000=329.555 ms; invalidate-only estimate=31.598 ms; diamond 128x2000=189.695 ms; sparse frontier proxy=0.428 ms; retained heap=6.855 ms/round; rewire churn=17.538 ms. Patch run: queue Vec/remove(0)=64.275 ms vs VecDeque=0.426 ms; fanout=598.892 ms; invalidate-only=97.417 ms; diamond=158.323 ms; sparse frontier proxy=0.454 ms; retained heap=14.758 ms/round; rewire churn=18.779 ms. The only meaningful win was diamond; fanout, invalidate-only, retained heap, sparse proxy, and rewire regressed, so the implementation was reverted per the probe gate. Conclusion: replacing closures mechanically is not enough; C is still post-1.0 and needs a smaller centralized engine that reduces per-delivery borrow/refcount/sort/token overhead, or it should not be pursued.

title: Rust product-completeness target: conformance parity is necessary but not sufficient; graphrefly-rs must also reach the current @graphrefly/ts feature surface.
trigger: Use at the start of future graphrefly-rs /dev-dispatch work. The Rust arm should continue from clean-slate with behavioral conformance parity (D24) as the protocol floor, while also implementing the product feature surface already landed in @graphrefly/ts: graph-first API, 8 verb sugar, sources, operators/combinators/higher-order/time/control/buffer families, reactive structures where sequenced, inspection/describe/observe/profile surfaces, and equivalent public ergonomics where appropriate. This is NOT structural parity: Rust may use Rust-native names/types/layouts and remains self-contained per D32; do not recreate the retired Impl/port model. If matching a TS feature reveals a protocol behavior gap or would change wave semantics, stop and route through spec-amend before code.
note: User clarification 2026-06-02: 'conformance parity' names only the cross-runtime behavioral contract; the roadmap expectation is fuller product completeness with @graphrefly/ts, not merely satisfying spec/conformance.jsonl. Next Rust sessions should not require this to be re-explained.
